It was great to see Darren Mead back in action over the country for the Bels. while 24 year-old Lee Hurst, on his début, took the chance to measure himself up against some of the London Lads.
Gary was back in the squad, returning from his pre-Christmas complete layoff. Lee Hurst was down from Manchester and raring to go while Roger Alsop and Jim Estall were known to be in cracking form.

At Clayton Vale, over 7 miles, the Greater Manchester Championships gave Lee Hurst the chance to fly the Belgrave flag. He finished just 3 seconds outside the medals as Sale's Kevin McKay grabbed 3rd in 36:49 to the Belgravian's 36:52.
Anyway, let's stop whinging and savour a fine run by Lee Hurst. Around 20th after the first loop, Lee worked his way through some of the top runners from the South of England.

Justin had jetted over from Houston, USA and welcomed new member and Inter-Counties Champion Lee Hurst who had flown in from Manchester, UK.

With Matt Yates chasing a World Cup place and producing a season's best to win the 1500m, plus maximum points from Justin Chaston and Lee Hurst in the steeplechase, and then further maximum points in the 5000m from Paul Evans and Kassa Tadessa, we looked invincible.

Our only other track win was by Lee Hurst in the 'A' Steeplechase, although Tom Lerwill only lost the 800 by a vest thickness (according to the official photograph) being given the same time of 1.49.19 as the winner – Justin Swift Smith of Shaftesbury Barnet.

The big improvements in: the Shot (Matt Simpson), 3000 Steeplechase (Justin Chaston and Lee Hurst), High Jump (Brendan Reilly), 5000 (Paul Evans), and 400H (Matt Douglas), show how big points can be accumulated by key individuals.

Dave Nolan's gold in the flat 400m, then Lee Hurst's silver in the steeplechase followed by wins for Matt Simson in the shot and Matt Yates in the 1500m increased our lead as Shaftesbury, Birchfield and Newham fought out the minor places.

And then it came together: Clive Gilby (took him longer to get there than he thought it would), Lee Hurst (with Carly having travelled from Manchester to Euston, to Waterloo, to Wimbledon), Ray Foley (with Anna and new baby Tess), Phil Carstairs (would he ever let us down) and others all arrived within a few minutes.

Among the Senior Men Lee Hurst quite obviously did not enjoy the mud and at 66th was well down on his 12th of last winter. Blackheath's Mark Steinle was up and away by the end of the first circuit and seemed to float over the morass to come home half a minute clear.

On March 14th 1998 at RoundhayPark, Leeds, Lee Hurst became holder of the Parker Bowl, awarded to the first Belgrave man home in the 'National'. Lee had a fine run to place30th in 47:07 with the race won by Shaftesbury Barnet's Dominic Bannister in 44:45. Other Belgrave placings in a field of 1661 finishers were: 252, G.Adams 52:05; 294, M.Webb 52:45; 439, P.Carstairs 54:30; 804, D.Anderson 58:47. Will Lee be first Belgravian again in 1999? Will we complete a team? You'll know by the time this magazine reaches you.

With Justin Chaston tied by work commitments in the USA, Lee Hurst was to prove a valuable choice for the steeplechase. No problems with the jumps squad until a week before departure, when Brendan Reilly was injured in a car crash and there was a last minute panic to get a visa for welcome newcomer…

Lee Hurst turned in his usual first class performance and newcomer Kevin Nash looked the part as he won the 'B' event. The match was well and truly won by the time the relays came round, which was just as well, as a combination of injuries and tiredness ensured that no records were in danger.

Lee Hurst reduced the deficit in the 3000 s/c and Jason Lobo pulled back more points to finish a fine second in the 1500m to Kevin McKay. Birchfield then came to our aid in the shot with an unknown American outthrowing Newham Mark Proctor with Matt Simson third.
